blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face little risk. A 2023 reform removed the sterilisation requirement for legal gender recognition (this was the last country in its region to drop it), but a medical statement is still required — not full self-determination. It issued a travel advisory for trans citizens travelling to a large destination country in March 2025.

The national police academy reports record hate-crime levels (1,808 suspected cases in 2024, up 13% since 2023 — the majority racist, but sexual orientation is among the identified motives). There are no documented severe trans-specific incidents (no tourist-rape, mob violence, or police-brutality case). Bathrooms are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation, and the regional visa-free border poses no trans-specific friction.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory beyond the update noted above; general urban crime is very low.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on this country: record 1,808 suspected hate crimes in 2025 (+13% since 2023), with sexual orientation and gender identity recurrent motives (12% of cases); the country's first conversion-practices case prosecuted as assault (convictions in March); parliament endorsed a citizens' initiative to ban conversion practices (125-49) in March, though a full ban remained pending.

The national police academy (Nov 2025): 1,808 suspected hate crimes reported to police in 2024 - the highest figure ever; defamation and assault most common; motive is decisive as the law does not recognise 'hate crime' as a distinct offence.

A foreign broadsheet (March 2025): this country and one neighbouring country updated travel advice urging caution for transgender people travelling to a large destination country amid its gender-document policy changes - the neighbour advised trans travellers to contact the destination's embassy before travel. Notable example of trans-specific official travel advisories.

A cross-border investigative journalism project (Sept 2025): investigation into sterilisation requirements for legal gender recognition across the region - thousands of trans people pushed into invasive surgery (including a case study of an orchiectomy required under another country's regional rules); this country is among those whose historical/current frameworks are examined.

National broadcaster (Feb 2018): this country's parliament approved recognising both women in same-sex partnerships as mothers from birth (122-42) - amending the maternity law to remove the adoption requirement for the non-birth mother.
National broadcaster (March 2017): the country's same-sex marriage law went into effect - same-sex couples also gained the right to adopt; ~41 couples scheduled to marry in the first week.
National broadcaster (Sept 2013): a citizens' initiative for same-sex marriage proceeded to parliament with 162,000 signatures - the largest citizens' initiative to date in this country.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2023 legal gender recognition reform (medical statement still required) is resident-facing.
